notes.content:
Additions and Changes:


 Slightly changed the Helmet hat model.
 Tweaked the Glide ability to be slightly more lenient when holding a few blocks.


Bugs Fixed:


 Adjusted an accidentally misplaced object in the Gallery Planetarium.
 Fixed a typo in the Records menu.
 Fixed a bug where the lighting in a certain deep area could be unintentionally bright under certain circumstances.
 Fixed a bug where portable checkpoint flags found in the Gallery were still able to be picked up after already collecting them.
 Fixed a bug where the entrance to the Gallery Planetarium could be locked shut if the player teleports inside rather than enters normally.

Bugs Fixed:

 Fixed a bug where active checkpoints didn’t change color to match yours if you changed it in the menu.
 Fixed a bug where one of the Gallery planetarium rooms was not set up correctly.
 Fixed some slightly incorrectly placed lava in a pipe.
 Fixed a bug where Toluti would sometimes not spawn outside Gates after completion even if he was with you when you entered. He’ll now be waiting for your return as intended.
 Altered the behavior of some launchpads to prevent a possible launch bug that sent the player much too far.
 Altered the material physics of ice picks to hopefully prevent accidental launches. Oops!

Additions and Changes:


 Tweaked some geometry in the Planetarium of the Gallery.
 Moved a block that was wedged inside a wood plank, resulting in getting stuck when picking it up.
 Slowed the speed of an archivist robot.
 Increased the size of certain ice cubes.
 Added a reward for scoring at basketball in the Gallery.
 Added bread.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where “Record Height” was not being saved when respawning from a checkpoint. It was only saving upon hitting a new checkpoint. It now saves properly at all times.
 Fixed a bug that was causing the skylight to not update until the end of weather transitions. It’s now much smoother as intended.

Minor Fixes

Bugs Fixed:

 Fixed a bug where an old glowing asset was visible in a dark place where it shouldn’t be.
 Fixed a but where a line of text was white when it should have been black.
 Removed an unintentional floating coral disc in the distant sky.

notes.title: Patch 1.1.07
notes.content:
Additions and Changes:


 Added a save data backup system. Every time you quit the game from the main menu, the game will save a backup version of your save data. In the event of data corruption due to power loss or other unexpected happenings, the game will detect the corruption and auto-restore from the backup save data. This change will not negatively affect existing save data.

notes.title: Minor Hotfix
notes.content: Just tweaking a glowing material that was not, in fact, glowing.

Additions and Changes:


 Added an additional ice pick somewhere.
 Adjusted a few minor geometry placements in one of the upper areas.


Bugs Fixed:


 Tweaked a music zone in a higher area that would sometimes stop playing the correct song if you went off the path a little bit.
 Tweaked a weather zone in a higher area that would sometimes be triggered incorrectly.
 Fixed a bug that caused Toluti to speak when he shouldn’t after a certain event.

Additions and Changes:


 Added a few easter eggs as a homage to a few players that have helped report bugs and make the game better. Find them in the Gallery shop.
 Renamed “Wizard” hat to “Occult” hat.
 Replaced a few hidden blocks with memory blocks in a few places.
 Adjusted some geometry just before entering the Cinders of Xorash to make a previously skippable ability now more essential for progression.
 Adjusted some geometry in the Cinders of Xorash.
 Adjusted some geometry just before entering the Xugan Caverns area.
 Adjusted the sound made by Crawlers when picked up to be less misleading. Also much less annoying. It was too much.
 Added a few more things that are affected by memory.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where an angled elevator would snap into the correct position upon activation, which could lead to launching the Ocnus off it.
 Fixed a bug where the title card when first reaching one of the checkpoints was incorrect.
 Fixed a bug where some planks were visible floating in the air when they shouldn’t have been.
 Fixed a bug where exiting screenshot mode while underwater would disable the underwater fog and visual effects until next entered/exited.
 Fixed a bug where Toluti would sometimes speak overlapping and incorrect dialogue lines when swapping Ocnus color.

Additions and Changes:


 Restored a bit of content that was cut from the game before release. I decided that I wanted it in the game after all. It’s only accessible after you’ve beaten the game as well as contained [REDACTED]. Find it at the peak, it might be worth a visit.
 Added some additional visual flair to the [REDACTED] area travelled to late in the game.
 Added an additional room to the Gallery, below the Elemental Orb exhibit.
 Added some additional water pools throughout the climb.
 Added some new bushes to a few biomes.
 Improved hanging bush visuals slightly.
 Improved vine visuals and added more vines.
 Increased the size of the small white flowers. Also added some yellow ones.
 Added some extra dirt/rock shapes to the bottoms of some larger islands in the tower.
 Added an elevator near the start of the game shortly after the first wooden tower.
 Adjusted 2 of the shortcut gem blocks to be more useful.
 Added some extra plant life to the Gallery.
 Updated the ability icons in the Guidebook.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where you could spin your camera around and slightly see inside the 100% completion room in the gallery before properly opening the gate.
 Fixed a bug during [REDACTED] where footstep sounds would play even while midair.
 Fixed a bug where a circular section of blocks near the peak was invisible.

Additions and Changes:


 Slightly optimized the post-processing materials used to make the camera rain distortion so they don’t use resources in the background when not active.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where unlocking a certain ability last did not grant the Research Complete achievement. It now will, and the game will double check this upon loading into the climb for anyone that this affected.
 Fixed a bug where a certain NPC in the Gallery would not randomly move around as intended. They now show up in random locations each time you go to the Gallery.
 Fixed a bug where the Completion text on a certain door in the Gallery remained visible even after opening the door.

Additions and Changes:


 Added a Render Distance setting to the options menu. Lowering it won’t do much on newer computers, but older hardware may benefit from lower distances.
 Slightly optimized all materials to run about 5-10% faster by removing unnecessary/unused features.
 Significantly optimized most translucent materials (especially water!) which should improve the performance of those materials by 30-40%. This will have more of an impact on older GPUs.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug in the “Launchers” challenge where the end flag collision box was raised too high off the ground, making it very hard to complete.
 Fixed a bug where the torii gate in one of the main menu themes was not functioning as intended.

Additions and Changes:


 Added some environmental support pillars/stones below the Toluti Trials starting area. No purpose, just aesthetic.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where the arm used to attach the elevator activation crystal to new elevators did not match the players Ocnus color properly.
 Fixed a bug where the squishing sound watermelons make upon breaking could be heard from any distance.
 Fixed a bug where the “Use Abilites” Idea for the Toluti Trials was not working as intended.
 Fixed a bug where the Toluti Trials gate near the top of the climb counted towards the tracker as an undiscovered item. It no longer pings.
 Fixed a bug where exiting to the main menu after finishing the first Toluti Trial and then doing a trial from the menu without first quitting the game would cause the abandon gate button to return you to the main level instead of the menu. It now properly updates and knows where to take you without requiring a reload.
 (Most likely) fixed a bug where a loud metal crashing sound could sometimes play unintentionally after hitting a certain switch every time the level is loaded.

notes.title: 1.1.0 - The Toluti Trials
notes.content:
The Toluti Trials:


 Added a new game mode called The Toluti Trials, which is unlockable by completing Toluti’s new questline.
 This mode is a semi-procedurally generated sandbox climbing challenge, with many randomized elements including which blocks you can use, weather, height, hazards, and many more.
 Most of these randomization settings can be tweaked to your liking in the menu.
 These trials contain unique hazards, blocks, and biomes that can only be found in this experimental zone.
 As you progress, you will find Inspiration. Once you earn enough Inspiration, it can becomes an Idea, unlocking new features for the mode and elsewhere.


Additions and Changes:


 Added a small new questline with the constructor head Toluti. You can access this once you have brought him high enough with you on your climb.
 Gave Toluti some additional dialogue near a few key locations.
 Added held block count to the HUD while in the Gallery, just like in the main climb level.
 Overhauled the 3D grass to make it blend properly with the terrain it’s growing from. It now matches the color and lighting more properly.
 Optimized the 3D grass models to use slightly less resources without losing detail.
 Increased the FOV from 35 to 45 when zoomed in with the Whip ability. It’s meant to be zoomed in, but it was a bit much.
 Changed the labels on the Gallery progress board to make it more clear which bars are for which type. Also changed the Colors model from a paint ball (as seen in the Gallery) to a paint pool (as seen in main climb level), as this is more likely what players will recognize.
 Changed some of the power switch buttons to be one-time presses rather than toggleable in instances where nobody would ever want to toggle them.
 Added a visual aid to checkered tile floors in the cathedral region to make it more apparent where you are when effected by them.
 Removed collision from the portable checkpoint flag tables that are created for Toluti to spawn on. They were able to cause the player to get trapped when placed in certain locations. The tables also now disappear once you grab Toluti.
 Adjusted the positioning of the title card sign at the start of the game during the first elevator to make it less likely to catch the player.
 Added a visual effect to the elevators to help communicate that it’s best to keep your arms and legs inside the vehicle at all times.
 Adjusted the wood planks on the rest platform near the end of the first biome to make it slightly easier to navigate.
 Reworded the Guidebook entry on abilities to make the stamina/cooldown system more clear to understand.
 Added a visual effect to the boats to help communicate which direction is currently being powered.
 Increased the size of the overlap zones on the boats, making them a bit easier to control when holding blocks.


Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where setting your hat back to “None” after putting on a hat did not visually update to remove the hat without reloading the level.
 Fixed a typo in one of the random loading screen messages: “didin’t” to “didn’t”. Oops!
 Fixed a rare bug with the Whip ability that could crash the game if you spammed it too often.
 Fixed a bug where the ground in a certain secret room was invisible.
 Fixed a bug where the hissing sound of extinguished candles could be heard regardless of distance.
 Fixed a bug where using the decode ability while being affected by checkered tile floors in the cathedral region would cause it to spawn in the ceiling/floor.
 Fixed a bug that allowed the decode ability to function without always requiring an additional input if spawned inside blocks. It will now only work when actually used as intended.
 Fixed a UI bug with controller input where you could leave a menu slider while editing it’s value, allowing you to navigate up and down to other buttons when you shouldn’t be able to.
 Fixed a bug with the torii gates that sometimes caused the hidden blocks to vanish much too soon.
 Adjusted how collisions are handled to reduce the chances of the Ocnus and any held blocks from sometimes becoming wedged inside moving objects when squished between them.

notes.title: 1.0.15.1 - Hotfix
notes.content:
Just a quick hotfix to replace a paint pool that was accidentally removed in preparation for future content. 

Oops! Sorry to all you color collectors out there!

Additions and Changes:


 Changed the order of Additions and Bugfixes in the patch notes. Makes more sense to talk about the new before talking about the fixed bugs. This is not, in fact, relevant to the game in any way.
 Added a few more seasonal props and moved some around.
 Strange monoliths have appeared throughout the climb, carved with old blueprints and maps. They point to something… deeper.
 Adjusted the warning text around the [REDACTED] to reflect changes in the state of the world once it has been interacted with.

Bugs Fixed:


 Fixed a bug where the Screen Effects option in the settings menu was not applying properly on level load. It now properly applies your saved settings.

This had no bearing on gameplay, achievements, or progression, but it broke something with the new map monoliths. notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
Hello all,

Xaeveax (Alex) here. I'm the developer of Ocnus Theory. It's been in development for a few years now and is finally reaching the finish line. I've been developing it part-time on the side of my full time job, so it's taken longer than perhaps it should have. 

This will be the first proper dev update I've done for the game, as it's largely been developed in isolation and secrecy. I've tried to keep things pretty close to the chest until the game was ready to release, and I can confidently say that the time is approaching shortly, hopefully by the end of the year. I am hoping for an August release window but it will largely depend on how QA testing goes.

As for actual development, I'm wrapping things up and putting the finishing touches on everything. The game itself is 95% finished. I'm in the QA testing phase, which is proving to be quite time consuming as a single, part-time developer. That said, things are coming along nicely and it's getting more and more polished with each play test. 

I'm hoping to start posting little tidbits of info about the game leading up to it's release, going over things like mechanics, locations, features, and maybe even some insight behind the development curtains. This will likely be here on Steam, though a future community Discord channel will be the place for more in-depth discussion. 

Some of the main things I'll be working on in the following weeks and months include:


Play testing the game many times and fixing any bugs I encounter.
Polishing up a few of the ability mechanics. These are unlocked as you progress, and some of the late-game ones really change up the game. I just need to make sure they work nicely across all locations.
Finishing up the lore notes. The game is focused on the gameplay, but the story/lore of the world does have quite a bit of depth to it and I need to make sure it's all communicated properly.
Challenge Mode polish. Some of the bonus challenge mode levels need a bit of love still, as they were built before some of the new ability mechanics were introduced.
 Sound effects work. Currently, the sounds played when dropping blocks, moving around, bumping into surfaces, etc. are all a bit unsatisfying. Due to the physics-driven nature of the game, designing the sounds for all of these interactions to take context into account takes more time than one might expect.
 Portable checkpoint bugfixing.  The portable checkpoint flag system works great, but there are a few things about them that need some serious special attention. It's a pretty important feature in the game, letting you place your own checkpoints (nearly) anywhere you want, so I want to make sure they function properly in all contexts.
 Performance on lower-end machines. The game runs buttery smooth on higher-end PCs, but lower end cards (testing on a GTX960 for example) proves to have some undesirable slowdown when on max settings. Of course, this can be solved by simply turning down some of the graphic options, but ideally I would like as many people as possible to be able to play it at 60 FPS. Despite the deceptively simple art style, the game does take advantage of lots of dynamic lights and precise physics, both of which take their toll in certain locations.


I'll try to keep things updated on here as I get closer to release. I'm also in the middle of setting up a community Discord server, which will be primarily for hearing feedback and discussing the game. I plan to continue to update the game post-release to improve it and add features that might be requested, so having a Discord will be a helpful tool to keep us all connected in that way.
